overview: Case-control study of adults who had day surgery between January 2025 and June 2026, with cases from the recovery nausea log and two controls per case from the same operating lists, classifying prophylaxis against the risk-tailored protocol from scanned anaesthetic records.
population: Cases: adults who received a rescue antiemetic in recovery or whose discharge was delayed by nausea or vomiting. Controls: two adults from the same operating list who did neither, chosen by a random number from the list. Excluded: planned overnight stays and procedures under local anaesthesia alone.
exposure: Prophylaxis relative to the protocol for the recorded risk score: under (fewer agents than recommended), matched, or over (more agents than recommended). Where the risk score is missing it is reconstructed from recorded risk factors and flagged.
procedures: Two anaesthesia fellows read the scanned records on hospital premises with a piloted extraction form: risk score and factors, antiemetics given, duration of surgery, intraoperative and recovery opioid dose, interpreter use. A random 10 percent of records are read by both fellows. Readers see the drug section before the recovery section, so exposure is classified before case status is visible where the scan order allows.

outcomes.name: Rescue treatment or delayed discharge for nausea or vomiting
outcomes.measure: Case status from the recovery nausea log and the discharge record
outcomes.why: The event patients and the unit want to prevent; reliably recorded (c3).

outcomes.name: Sedation delaying discharge
outcomes.measure: Recorded sedation or drowsiness as the reason for delayed discharge, in all sampled patients

outcomes.name: Adherence among controls
outcomes.measure: Proportion of controls whose prophylaxis matched the protocol
outcomes.why: Estimates adherence in patients who did well, which the unit has never seen.

feasibility: About 546 records at about six minutes each is about 55 hours, within the 60 hours available; access under HR-2026-118.
biasMitigation: Controls from the same operating list
Exposure classified from the drug section before recovery notes where possible
Double reading of a random 10 percent of records
Adjustment for risk score, duration of surgery and opioid dose fixed before extraction

biasFlags.label: Confounding by indication
biasFlags.note: Sicker patients and longer operations receive more prophylaxis; adjustment and list matching limit this.

biasFlags.label: Case under-ascertainment
biasFlags.note: The log misses some rescue treatments at the end of busy days.

biasFlags.label: Reader awareness of case status
biasFlags.note: Order of reading and double reading reduce it.

flags: Three adjustment variables fixed before extraction
parsimony.simplestPath: One exposure in three levels, one primary outcome, three covariates, list-matched controls.

summary: Case-control protocol with list-matched controls, one primary outcome, a sedation outcome and a process measure; no theoretical framework is used.
